summary: Hideyo Ogawa is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Hiroshima University (~1973–1982). He spent his career at Hiroshima University, serving as an assistant professor (~1989–1997) and as Professor of Indian Philosophy (~1997–2020).
Hideyuki Matsumori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a doctoral student at Soka University (attested 2006) and later held an assistant post (助教) there (attested 2015).
Hildegard Diemberger is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who completed supervised studies under Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner.

Himanshu Prabha Ray is an Indology and archaeology scholar educated at Panjab University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Cambridge. She served as Associate Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1980–2012) and Chairperson of the National Monuments Authority (2012–2015).

Hinrich Middeldorpf (1788–1861) was a linguistics and religious studies scholar. After studying at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums and the University of Göttingen (~1806–1810), he served on the faculty at the University of Breslau from circa 1813 to 1861.

Hiralal Rasikdas Kapadia, working in Indology and religious studies, served as Professor of Ardhamagadhi at MTB Arts College and as a University Teacher for Ph.D. students in Ardhamagadhi at the University of Mumbai (both attested 1947).

Hiram W. Woodward is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard and Yale. He held posts at the University of Michigan, the University of Vermont, and the Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri (1878–1946) was an Indologist and archaeologist educated at Oriental College and Panjab University. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India, as Government Epigraphist (attested 1931), and as Director of Archaeology for Baroda State (1934–1942).
Hiroaki Yokoyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2013) and later held a post there as a research student (研究生).

Hirofumi Isoda is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University by 1966. He later served as lecturer (attested 1972) and Associate Professor (attested 1989–2000) at Tohoku University.
Hirofumi Toda (1936–2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seiren Matsunami (~1959–1965) and served as a professor at Tokushima University (~1978–2002).
Hiroko Kawanami is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott. She held a post as senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).
Hiroko Matsuoka is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University (attested 2006) and later held a post at the University of Leipzig (attested 2016).

Hiromasa Tosaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Kyushu and Harvard Universities under scholars including Seiren Matsunami and Daniel H. H. Ingalls, he served as a professor at Kyushu University from circa 1975 to 1994.
Hiromi Habata is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Freiburg. She held a research post at the University of Munich (attested 2014).
Hiromi Yoshimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who served on the faculty at Ryukoku University, including as a full-time lecturer (attested 1987) and in a later post attested in 2006.
Hiromu Kitanishi (1925–2019) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Otani University (~1944–1948) and later served as a professor there from circa 1968 to 1991.
Hironori Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at Bukkyo University (attested 2015–2020) and subsequently held a post there.

Hiroo Kashiwagi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963). He served as a professor at Matsusaka University (~1982–2000) and president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College (~1989–1998).

Hiroo Sato is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1973–1984). He held posts at Morioka College (~1987–1993) and as Professor at Tohoku University (~2001–2019).
